evidence.claim: China joined a P5 statement that says nuclear war must never be fought, nuclear weapons should be defensive, and the spread of such weapons must be prevented.
evidence.title: JOINT STATEMENT Of the Leaders of the Five Nuclear-Weapon States On Preventing Nuclear War and Avoiding Arms Races
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China
evidence.excerpt: China joined a P5 statement that says nuclear war must never be fought, nuclear weapons should be defensive, and the spread of such weapons must be prevented.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official text with dated leadership-level language and direct nuclear-risk commitments.
evidence.period_fit: Direct January 2022 nuclear-risk statement, strong period fit.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Xi only as part of China's top leadership role inside a joint P5 act, not as a unilateral Chinese order.
contrary_evidence: The statement is declaratory and does not by itself prove later restraint.
Later-2022 force build-up complicates the restraint message.

evidence.claim: The Congress called for enhanced political loyalty in the military and faster modernization of strategic capabilities.
evidence.title: Full text of resolution on 19th CPC Central Committee report
evidence.excerpt: The Congress called for enhanced political loyalty in the military and faster modernization of strategic capabilities.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official congress resolution with explicit military guidance.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Collective party resolution under Xi's leadership, with direct relevance to his authority over the military.
contrary_evidence: It is a broad military modernization mandate, not a nuclear-safety reform.
It does not mention arms control or de-escalation.

evidence.claim: Xi secured a precedent-breaking third term and introduced a top governing body stacked with loyalists, cementing his dominance over the party.
evidence.title: China's Xi clinches third term, packs leadership with loyalists
evidence.excerpt: Xi secured a precedent-breaking third term and introduced a top governing body stacked with loyalists, cementing his dominance over the party.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire item with direct reporting on the post-congress leadership lineup.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Xi's consolidation of authority, though the article is still journalistic analysis.
contrary_evidence: Leadership loyalty is not the same as nuclear expertise.
Centralization can increase control but also reduce internal challenge and corrective dissent.

evidence.claim: China launched its largest-ever drills around Taiwan, fired missiles near the island, and sharply raised the risk of regional miscalculation after Pelosi's visit.
evidence.title: Furious China fires missiles near Taiwan in drills after Pelosi visit
evidence.excerpt: China launched its largest-ever drills around Taiwan, fired missiles near the island, and sharply raised the risk of regional miscalculation after Pelosi's visit.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire item, even though the republisher page title is noisy.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Xi's governing system and Taiwan policy, though the article reports military action rather than a direct Xi quote.
contrary_evidence: The drills were conventional, not nuclear use.
They may be read as signaling rather than immediate escalation to nuclear brinkmanship.

evidence.claim: China suspended military and climate dialogue with the United States after Pelosi's Taiwan trip, including military-to-military contacts.
evidence.title: China halts military, climate dialogue with U.S. over Pelosi Taiwan trip
evidence.excerpt: China suspended military and climate dialogue with the United States after Pelosi's Taiwan trip, including military-to-military contacts.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire item reporting the break in dialogue channels.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Chinese state under Xi, but not a personal nuclear command act.
contrary_evidence: The suspension may have been temporary.
The article does not prove the duration or full collapse of all channels.

evidence.claim: U.S. officials said China showed no interest in discussing steps to reduce nuclear risk after Xi signaled in October that Beijing would strengthen its strategic deterrent.
evidence.title: U.S. says China resisting nuclear talks after Xi vow to boost deterrent
evidence.excerpt: U.S. officials said China showed no interest in discussing steps to reduce nuclear risk after Xi signaled in October that Beijing would strengthen its strategic deterrent.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire item reporting on U.S.-China arms-control contact in November 2022.
evidence.period_fit: Strong late-2022 fit, tied to Xi's October congress line.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant to Xi because the U.S. response is tied to his public strategic-deterrence signal.
contrary_evidence: This is U.S. official interpretation, not a Chinese admission.
It reports interest in talks, not a formal Chinese refusal document.

evidence.claim: The Pentagon projected that China could reach 1,500 nuclear warheads by 2035 if its build-up pace continues, and linked that assessment to Xi's October deterrent signal.
evidence.title: China nuclear warhead stockpile to reach 1,500 by 2035 if it continues its build-up pace, US says
evidence.excerpt: The Pentagon projected that China could reach 1,500 nuclear warheads by 2035 if its build-up pace continues, and linked that assessment to Xi's October deterrent signal.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters-based reporting of the Pentagon's annual China military assessment.
evidence.period_fit: Targets the 2022 force trajectory and end-of-year posture.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Xi as the top political authority overseeing the force expansion, though the projection is U.S. analysis.
contrary_evidence: The article says the build-up was brisk but not necessarily accelerating in that moment.
U.S. projections carry uncertainty and may overstate near-term deployment status.

evidence.claim: The two sides held a constructive discussion to maintain open channels of communication between the Department of Defense and the People's Liberation Army under the 2014 military-notification MOU.
evidence.title: U.S. and PRC Hold Working Level Meeting on DoD 2022 Annual Report
evidence.excerpt: The two sides held a constructive discussion to maintain open channels of communication between the Department of Defense and the People's Liberation Army under the 2014 military-notification MOU.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official U.S. statement on a specific bilateral military-channel meeting.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in late 2022, after the Pelosi crisis and before year-end.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirectly attributable to Xi-era governance because the PLA and CMC were the Chinese counterpart, but not a direct Xi act.
contrary_evidence: The meeting was bilateral and procedural, not proof of broad de-escalation.
It does not show that all crisis channels remained open.

evidence.claim: China told the First Committee that it had pledged no-first-use against non-nuclear states, kept its forces at the minimum required for national security, and did not engage in an arms race.
evidence.title: World Must Step Back from Brink of Nuclear Madness Amid Growing Risk of Miscalculation, Accidental Use, First Committee Told
evidence.excerpt: China told the First Committee that it had pledged no-first-use against non-nuclear states, kept its forces at the minimum required for national security, and did not engage in an arms race.
evidence.source_locator: Li Song statement in press release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UN meeting record quoting the Chinese delegate in a formal multilateral setting.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is official Chinese policy language under Xi, but still declaratory rather than operational conduct.
contrary_evidence: The statement is self-reported and non-verifiable on its own.
It coexists with visible force expansion and tougher Taiwan signaling.

evidence.claim: China's delegate denounced strengthening rivalries and cooperation on nuclear submarines while reaffirming no-first-use and rejection of competitive arms racing.
evidence.title: With Risk of Armageddon, Apocalypse from Just One Single Nuclear Detonation, General Assembly Members Reaffirm Determination to Eliminate Such Weapons
evidence.excerpt: China's delegate denounced strengthening rivalries and cooperation on nuclear submarines while reaffirming no-first-use and rejection of competitive arms racing.
evidence.source_locator: press release summary of the China intervention
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UN meeting record summarizing the Chinese intervention at the review conference.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the 2022 NPT review conference calendar.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Official Chinese position, not an independent monitoring claim.
contrary_evidence: It remains declaratory and does not show substantive arms-control progress.
The intervention does not resolve concerns raised by China's force expansion.

evidence.claim: The revised Party Constitution adds language on enhancing political loyalty in the military, strengthening the military through reform and science and technology, and keeping the armed forces under centralized Party leadership.
evidence.title: Full text of resolution on Party Constitution amendment
evidence.excerpt: The revised Party Constitution adds language on enhancing political loyalty in the military, strengthening the military through reform and science and technology, and keeping the armed forces under centralized Party leadership.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official party text with clear institutional implications.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Xi's institutional design, though not a standalone personal nuclear act.
contrary_evidence: This is about political control and military modernization, not direct nuclear safety reform.
It says nothing about safeguarding against accidental escalation.

unresolved_gaps: Direct command-and-control, custody, and launch-discipline evidence is still thin.
Concrete arms-control follow-through beyond declaratory no-first-use language is limited.
Crisis de-escalation evidence in the Taiwan and Russia-Ukraine settings is mostly indirect.
Direct evidence of Xi personally authorizing or restraining specific military moves is thin.
Civilian-protection and operational-conduct evidence during the Taiwan crisis is limited.
Evidence of actual mediation or de-escalation in Russia-Ukraine remains mostly declaratory.
Water, sanitation, and local service-variation evidence is thin compared with health, pensions, housing, and crisis response.
Chain-of-command evidence for specific repression episodes remains limited.
Independent evidence on courts, legislatures, and oversight bodies resisting capture is thin.
Succession and term-limit mechanics could be more directly documented as a de facto transfer-rule breach.
Independent evaluation of implementation quality across provinces and local-government debt stress remains limited.
Distributional evidence beyond averages and poverty-lifted subgroups could be stronger.
Water/sanitation and housing-quality evidence is thinner than health, pensions, and child-welfare evidence.
Independent evaluation of service quality, regional equity, and front-line delivery remains limited.
Direct, ruler-specific evidence on Xi's own assets, gifts, family business interests, or beneficial ownership is missing.
Independent findings on concealment or obstruction tied personally to Xi are absent.
Evidence of truthful correction versus rhetorical anti-corruption messaging is weak.
Independent evaluation of whether loyalist-heavy appointments improved competence or mainly tightened political control is thin.
More subnational evidence on execution quality and correction would strengthen the adaptation story.
Durable causal impact of the COVID rollback and economic stabilization package remains under-audited.
